question: When one shared standard connects all AI tools, who gets to shape the rules?
reflection: Shared standards can let small builders reach many users at once, if no single company quietly controls the gate.

sources.subject: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol, OpenAI Agent Plugins Standard, Block Buzz Work

one_line: OpenAI is moving from shipping models to setting the shared format that agent tools across many companies will use.

top_stories.title: One plugin format for many agents
top_stories.what: OpenAI launched an open format for packaging agent skills and connectors, with Google, Amazon, Microsoft and others on its steering group.
top_stories.why: A shared format means a tool built once for one client could work in many AI assistants.

top_stories.title: ChatGPT gets a more careful default
top_stories.what: OpenAI says its new default paid model makes far fewer factual errors in finance, health and law questions and disagrees with users when they are wrong.
top_stories.why: Less flattery from AI matters for research use, where agreeable answers can bias conclusions.

top_stories.title: A workspace shared by people and agents
top_stories.what: Block released Buzz, a free self-hosted workspace where AI agents join chat rooms with their own identity, permissions and records.
top_stories.why: Giving agents the same permission rules as staff is a practical model for workplace pilots.

saudi_lens.text: A self-hosted workspace with agents could suit Saudi organisations that cannot send internal chats to foreign cloud services.

idea.title: Agent teammate trial
idea.pitch: Run a four-week trial where one AI agent joins a project channel with limited permissions, and measure how staff use and trust it.
idea.first_step: Write a one-page list of what the agent may read, write and never touch.

idea_kids.title: Universal plug puzzle
idea_kids.pitch: A building activity where children design one plug shape that fits several different toy machines, learning why shared rules help.
idea_kids.first_step: Cut cardboard machines with different sockets and challenge groups to design one shared plug.
